text.p: Italian bond futures moved higher in early trading supported by the sharp overnight rise in U.S. T-bonds and the firmer tone early to German bunds while data on Italian wage inflation showed a steady trend, dealers said.

They added that the market lead came for abroad after the spectacular rise of around one and a half full points in T-bonds after friendly data eased inflation fears and some thought put back the date of a further U.S. interest rate rise.
"The direction is coming from the U.S. with little fresh news on the domestic front, but trading is set to be quiet ahead of a holiday in much of Europe tomorrow," said one dealer.
The U.S. reported first quarter employment costs rose just 0.6 percent against 0.9 percent predicted on Tuesday in a report the Federal Reserve watches closely when setting U.S. rates.
In Italy, ISTAT reported annual wage inflation in Italy was steady at 4.5 percent in March, unchanged for the 4.5 percent level seen the previous month.

Dealers said that BTP futures are likely to look to push firmer with one eye on how the U.S. markets open later today, but trading likely to be cautious head of May Day holiday on Thursday in Italy and much of Europe. LIFFE market in London trading BTP futures will be open Thursday.
Later today, the Italian Treasury holds the second day of its end-month auction of 2.5 trillion lire worth of three-year BTPs and 3.0 trillion lire of five-year BTPs.
